out.other_title: Weak-to-strong generalization: weak model labels partially elicit strong model capability
out.rationale: Burns et al. report strong models naively finetuned on weak-model labels outperform their supervisors but, with naive finetuning alone, fall far short of full capability, and that simple methods such as an auxiliary confidence loss can often significantly improve weak-to-strong generalization. Wen et al. report ICM, using no external labels, matches golden-label training and outperforms crowdsourced human supervision on GSM8K-verification, TruthfulQA and Alpaca reward modeling; one uses labels from a weak model, the other self-generated labels, and model families differ.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: how to elicit a strong pretrained model's capabilities without strong (human-level or better) supervision

text: The authors introduce Internal Coherence Maximization (ICM), an unsupervised algorithm that fine-tunes pretrained language models on their own generated labels without external supervision. They report that on GSM8k-verification, TruthfulQA and Alpaca reward modeling ICM matches training on golden labels and outperforms crowdsourced human supervision, that it elicits strongly superhuman capabilities better than human labels, and that an RL-trained Claude 4 Sonnet-based assistant using an ICM reward model matches its counterpart trained on production-grade human labels on average, with higher chat and safety scores and lower math and coding scores.
title: Internal Coherence Maximization (ICM): unsupervised elicitation matches golden labels
